_meta.description: Adversarial DSL corpus for server/tools/guardrails.ts, run by eval/run_lint.js against the COMPILED guardrails module (path via EVAL_GUARDRAILS_JS -- see eval/README.md).
_meta.pipeline_order_note: executor.ts's executeIndexerRequest runs checkIndexAllowlist(index) FIRST, then applySafetyValves(body), then lintDsl(valved.body, index) -- in that order. run_lint.js replicates that exact order per case so 'reject' cases are attributed to the correct function/reason. lintDsl no longer takes a `toolName` 3rd argument as of the 5.0 port (the get_solved_vulnerabilities tool it used to exempt was retired, so the vulnerability-field-on-a-time-based-index check has no per-tool carve-out anymore).
_meta.expect_values: reject: the relevant function must return {ok:false}, with `reason` matching `reason_match`. clamp: the relevant function must return {ok:true} AND the named field(s) in `body` (after applySafetyValves) must equal the documented clamp value. pass: every function in the pipeline for this case must return {ok:true} (silent field rewrites like a forced track_total_hits are expected and not a failure).

cases.name: script_in_query
cases.citation: guardrails.ts:97-103 findKey(body,'script') walks the full tree (guardrails.ts:127-144) and rejects on ANY key literally named "script", anywhere.

cases.name: script_fields
cases.citation: guardrails.ts's comment (line 3-4, 98) names script_fields explicitly, but the CODE only ever checks for a literal "script" key (findKey, guardrails.ts:146-154); this case is rejected because real OpenSearch script_fields syntax nests an actual "script" key inside each field entry, not because "script_fields" itself is special-cased.

cases.name: runtime_mappings
cases.citation: Same mechanism as script_fields above: guardrails.ts never checks for a "runtime_mappings" key specifically, but the field definition nests a real "script" key, so findKey(body,'script') (guardrails.ts:97) still catches it.

cases.name: regexp_query
cases.citation: guardrails.ts:110-112 -- findKey(body,'regexp') hard-blocks unconditionally, no allowlist.

cases.name: leading_wildcard_wildcard_clause
cases.citation: guardrails.ts:86-88 LEADING_WILDCARD_KEYS includes 'wildcard'; guardrails.ts:169-180 findLeadingWildcard walks the tree and flags any string value starting with * or ? (or after whitespace/(/: per LEADING_WILDCARD_PATTERN, guardrails.ts:88).

cases.name: leading_wildcard_query_string_clause
cases.citation: guardrails.ts:86 LEADING_WILDCARD_KEYS also includes 'query_string' (and 'simple_query_string') -- this is exactly the 4.14 pattern get_suspicious_powershell.ts documents having to route around.

cases.name: date_range_over_90_days
cases.citation: guardrails.ts:83 MAX_LOOKBACK_MS = 90*24*60*60*1000; guardrails.ts:226-231 rejects when lteMs-gteMs exceeds it. now-180d resolves via resolveDateMath (guardrails.ts:182-198, the now-Nd/h/m branch) to 180 days before 'now', comfortably over the cap.

cases.name: time_range_missing_lte_bound
cases.citation: guardrails.ts:212-214 -- a range on a recognized time field (TIME_FIELD_RE, guardrails.ts:82, matches 'timestamp' or '@timestamp') with only one of gte/lte present is rejected outright, regardless of span.

cases.name: no_time_range_at_all_on_time_index
cases.citation: lintDsl now takes the target index and rejects any query against a time-based index (TIME_BASED_INDEX_RE, wazuh-events-v5-*/wazuh-findings-v5-* as of the 5.0 port) that contains no range clause on a time field at all (hasTimeRange walk). wazuh-states-* stays exempt -- see states_index_no_time_range_still_passes.

cases.name: states_index_no_time_range_still_passes
cases.citation: Regression guard for the mandatory-time-bound check's exemption: wazuh-states-* indices are current-state snapshots with no event-time axis (guardrails.ts TIME_BASED_INDEX_RE matches only wazuh-events-v5-*/wazuh-findings-v5-* as of the 5.0 port), so a rangeless query against them must keep passing -- this is the shape of get_critical_vulnerabilities.ts's real query.

cases.name: size_over_500_clamped
cases.citation: guardrails.ts:53-54 -- next.size = Math.min(Math.max(requestedSize,0), MAX_SIZE=500) -- 5000 clamps to 500, applySafetyValves still returns ok:true (this is a silent rewrite, not a rejection).

cases.name: track_total_hits_always_forced
cases.citation: guardrails.ts:55 -- next.track_total_hits = MAX_TRACK_TOTAL_HITS (10000) unconditionally, overwriting whatever the caller sent (true, false, or a number) every single time.

cases.name: from_deep_pagination_rejected
cases.citation: guardrails.ts:12,42-50 -- MAX_FROM=1000; from>1000 is a hard rejection (not a clamp) inside applySafetyValves, before lintDsl even runs (executor.ts:92-100 order).

cases.name: terms_agg_non_allowlisted_field
cases.reason_match: not on the allowed low-cardinality field list
cases.citation: guardrails.ts:64-80 AGG_FIELD_ALLOWLIST does not include data.srcip (a genuinely high-cardinality field); guardrails.ts:244-249 checkAggs rejects any terms/cardinality/significant_terms agg whose field isn't on that allowlist.

cases.name: terms_agg_size_over_100
cases.citation: guardrails.ts:84 MAX_AGG_SIZE=100; guardrails.ts:251-253 checkAggs rejects when an allowlisted field's terms agg 'size' still exceeds 100 (rule.id itself IS allowlisted, guardrails.ts:65, so only the size trips this one).

cases.name: index_not_on_allowlist
cases.citation: guardrails.ts INDEX_ALLOWLIST_RE = /^wazuh-(events-v5|findings-v5|states)[^,\s]*$/ (5.0 port; wazuh-alerts-*/wazuh-archives-* were dropped from the allowlist) -- wazuh-monitoring-* (agent connection-status history, a real Wazuh index family) is deliberately outside the three-family allowlist and is rejected by checkIndexAllowlist before applySafetyValves/lintDsl ever run.

cases.name: bool_must_normalized_to_filter
cases.citation: applySafetyValves now runs normalizeMustToFilter (recursive, copy-on-write) -- every bool.must's entries are appended to that bool's filter array and the must key removed, making the escape hatch's 'filter context' contract true by normalization instead of a rejection round-trip. Matching semantics identical (scoring-only difference); should/must_not deliberately untouched. This case asserts the moved clause lands at filter[1] (after the pre-existing filter[0]) and that must is gone.

cases.name: clean_query_filter_context_time_bounded
cases.citation: Shape of get_critical_alerts.ts:34-46's real, in-production query -- must pass cleanly end to end (checkIndexAllowlist, applySafetyValves, lintDsl all ok:true).

cases.name: clean_aggregation_query
cases.citation: Shape of get_top_rules.ts:32-44's real, in-production aggregation query (minus the top_hits sub-agg, irrelevant to guardrails) -- rule.id is allowlisted and size is well under the 100 cap.

cases.name: time_range_in_should_bypasses_mandatory_check
cases.citation: A decorative should-range runs unbounded (measured at 2272 full-corpus docs vs 1650 bounded), so hasTimeRange only credits a time range in REQUIRED context (bool.filter/must), not bool.should — a decorative should-range no longer satisfies the mandatory bound.

cases.name: time_range_in_must_not_bypasses_mandatory_check
cases.citation: Must_not variant: a negated range EXCLUDES the window, worse than decorative). Same required-context fix as time_range_in_should_bypasses_mandatory_check.

cases.name: multi_terms_agg_bypasses_field_allowlist
cases.reason_match: not on the allowed low-cardinality field list
cases.citation: (returns data.srcip buckets with size 10000 honored). checkAggs now iterates multi_terms.terms[].field against AGG_FIELD_ALLOWLIST and checks multi_terms.size.

cases.name: composite_agg_size_never_checked
cases.citation: . agent.id is allowlisted so only composite.size=10000 trips the check, which the composite branch now enforces against MAX_AGG_SIZE.

cases.name: date_histogram_tiny_interval_bucket_explosion
cases.citation: (cluster backstops at max_buckets=65535->503, but wastes compute). checkAggs now enforces a >=1m interval floor on date_histogram/histogram.

cases.name: query_string_leading_wildcard_behind_plus_operator
cases.citation: (ran 3.4s as an expensive leading-wildcard scan). LEADING_WILDCARD_PATTERN boundary class now includes the Lucene operators + - ! ^ ~.

cases.name: index_allowlist_comma_smuggling
cases.citation: /latent (not reachable today: index is enum-locked in schema_validator). INDEX_ALLOWLIST_RE now rejects a comma/whitespace-smuggled disallowed index appended after a valid prefix.

cases.name: vuln_field_match_on_alerts_index_rejected
cases.reason_match: Vulnerability data is not in the findings/events index
cases.citation: Observed against the 4.14 equivalent of this query: this is the shape of escape-hatch query the model hand-builds instead of calling a typed vulnerability tool. guardrails.ts's findVulnerabilityFieldOnAlertsIndex (called from lintDsl, before the mandatory-time-range check) rejects any match/match_phrase/term/terms/range/exists clause on a data.vulnerability.*/vulnerability.* field against a time-based (wazuh-events-v5-*/wazuh-findings-v5-*) index, naming the typed vulnerability tools so the model self-corrects in the same turn. The 5.0 port retired both get_solved_vulnerabilities and its per-tool exemption on this check (lintDsl no longer takes a toolName argument), so this rejection is now unconditional on a time-based index -- there is no legitimate caller of vulnerability fields on the findings/events timeline.

cases.name: vuln_field_match_on_states_index_still_passes
cases.citation: Regression guard against overreach for vuln_field_match_on_alerts_index_rejected: the check keys on TIME_BASED_INDEX_RE (wazuh-events-v5-*/wazuh-findings-v5-* only, as of the 5.0 port), so the exact same field filter against wazuh-states-vulnerabilities-* -- the real current-state index every vulnerability tool targets -- must never be rejected by this rule. wazuh-states-* is also exempt from the mandatory-time-range check (see states_index_no_time_range_still_passes), so this case passes end to end.
